Slide.Title: face (noun)
Slide.SlideText: face (noun) Definition: Definition: the front of the head, including the eyes, nose, mouth, etc. Synonyms: Synonyms: countenance; features; mug (informal) Examples: Examples: Those twin brothers have similar faces. You have some spaghetti sauce on your face. The baby has a cute face. The baby has a cute face.

Slide.Title: face (verb)
Slide.SlideText: face (verb) Definition: Definition: 1) to turn toward a particular direction; 2) to accept the reality; 3) to have a difficult situation to deal with Synonyms: Synonyms: align; 2) confront; accept Examples: Examples: The largest bedroom faces south. (align) We have to face the fact that the company is losing money. (accept) He’s facing a challenge. (confront) He’s facing a challenge.

Slide.Title: factory(noun)
Slide.SlideText: factory(noun) Definition: Definition: a building where products are made Synonyms: Synonyms: plant Examples: Examples: The tire factory employs 250 people. There are many factories in this part of the city. He’s making spare parts in a car factory. A modern factory is totally automated. He’s making spare parts in a car factory.

Slide.Title: fail (verb)
Slide.SlideText: fail (verb) Definition: Definition: to not succeed; to not reach a goal Synonyms: Synonyms: flop (informal) Examples: Examples: He passed one test but failed the other. This new technology cannot fail, can it? Will he succeed or fail? Sometimes, you must fail before you succeed. Sometimes, you must fail before you succeed.

Slide.Title: fair (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: fair (adjective) Definition: Definition: not favoring one person or another; equal Synonyms: Synonyms: just; equitable; impartial Examples: Examples: Children get upset when things are not fair. It’s fair if they get equal pay for the same job. It is fair to say that both balls are of equal weight. It is fair to say that both balls are of equal weight.

Slide.Title: famous (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: famous (adjective) Definition: Definition: well known to many people Synonyms: Synonyms: celebrated; renowned; prominent Examples: Examples: Elvis Presley is one of the most famous singers. Donald Trump is a famous business person. The famous building, the Taj Mahal, is in India. Would you like to be famous? Would you like to be famous?

Slide.Title: fan (noun)
Slide.SlideText: fan (noun) Definition: Definition: a person who loves a sport, activity or performer Synonyms: Synonyms: admirer; follower; devotee Examples: Examples: Who has more fans, Celine Dion or Mariah Carey? He’s a fan of simple home design. We are all fans of the baseball game. We’re all fans of the baseball game.

Slide.Title: favorite (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: favorite (adjective) Definition: Definition: person or thing that is liked most of all or preferred to all others Synonyms: Synonyms: preferred; desired Examples: Examples: Who is your favorite author? Her favorite singer is always changing. What’s your favorite movie? He is eating his favorite ice cream! He is eating his favorite ice cream!

Slide.Title: fence (noun)
Slide.SlideText: fence (noun) Definition: Definition: something around an area of land to keep animals or people in or out Synonyms: Synonyms: boundary; barrier; enclosure Examples: Examples: They want to build a fence around their home. How high should a home fence be? She loves her bamboo fence. She loves her bamboo fence.

Slide.Title: field (noun)
Slide.SlideText: field (noun) Definition: Definition: 1) an area of open land; 2) an area of study such as law, medicine, etc. Synonyms: Synonyms: 1) meadow; 2) subject Examples: Examples: His field of study is law (subject) A green field is a beautiful field. This is a beautiful field of lavender in France (meadow) This is a beautiful field of lavender in France.

Slide.Title: final (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: final (adjective) Definition: Definition: at the end; last Synonyms: Synonyms: last; concluding; ending Examples: Examples: He is taking his final exam. What were her final words? They are in the final part of the race. The final piece was placed in the puzzle. The final piece was placed in the puzzle.

Slide.Title: financial (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: financial (adjective) Definition: Definition: connected with money; relating to or involving money Synonyms: Synonyms: monetary; fiscal, economic Examples: Examples: They are facing financial problems. What do you do when you have a financial disagreement in your family? Financial decisions are very important.. Financial decisions are very important..

Slide.Title: find (verb)
Slide.SlideText: find (verb) Definition: Definition: to discover something or someone after a search Synonyms: Synonyms: discover; recover; locate Examples: Examples: Did you find your keys? They need to find an apartment in the city. They found each other. He was lucky to find his keys! He was lucky to find his keys!

Slide.Title: fine (noun)
Slide.SlideText: fine (noun) Definition: Definition: a payment to punish someone for a crime Synonyms: Synonyms: penalty Examples: Examples: How much is the fine for speeding? Sam had to pay a fine because he parked in the wrong place. Sam had to pay a fine because he parked in the wrong place.

Slide.Title: finish (verb)
Slide.SlideText: finish (verb) Definition: Definition: to complete; to end Synonyms: Synonyms: conclude; end Examples: Examples: She could not finish her dinner. When will you finish your work? He finished the race. He finished the race.

Slide.Title: fit (verb)
Slide.SlideText: fit (verb) Definition: Definition: to be the right size or shape Synonyms: Synonyms: right size Examples: Examples: That desk does not fit in this room. These shoes fit perfectly. Their jeans do not fit. Their jeans do not fit.

Slide.Title: fix (verb)
Slide.SlideText: fix (verb) Definition: Definition: to repair, mend or correct something Synonyms: Synonyms: repair; mend Examples: Examples: How much will it cost to fix the car? Can you fix our sink? He can fix the heater. He can fix the heater.

Slide.Title: float (verb)
Slide.SlideText: float (verb) Definition: Definition: 1) to be on a liquid without sinking; 2) to move or be moved gently on a liquid or through air Synonyms: Synonyms: 1) drift; 2) glide Examples: Examples: I love to float on the water. (drift) The balloon floated down the street. (glide) An astronaut can float in space. (glide) An astronaut can float in space.

Slide.Title: floor (noun)
Slide.SlideText: floor (noun) Definition: Definition: 1) the bottom part of a room where people walk; 2) each level of a building Synonyms: Synonyms: 1) flooring; 2) story Examples: Examples: How many floors does that building have? (story) My favorite floor is hard wood. (flooring) Marble floors are beautiful. (flooring) A wood floor is beautiful. (flooring) A wood floor is beautiful.

Slide.Title: fluid (noun)
Slide.SlideText: fluid (noun) Definition: Definition: a liquid Synonyms: Synonyms: liquid Examples: Examples: How many fluids are used in a car? Some fluid is leaking into our office. We should drink 64 ounces of fluids a day. Water, in it’s natural state, is a fluid. Water, in its natural state, is a fluid.

Slide.Title: fly (verb)
Slide.SlideText: fly (verb) Definition: Definition: move through the air using wings or an airplane Synonyms: Synonyms: soar Examples: Examples: Do you fly frequently? Birds often fly together. This airplane from the 1940’s still flies. This airplane from the 1940’s still flies.

Slide.Title: follow (verb)
Slide.SlideText: follow (verb) Definition: Definition: to come or go after Synonyms: Synonyms: trail; pursue Examples: Examples: She followed her friend to the hotel because she did not know the area. Her dog follows her everywhere. People will follow a good leader. People will follow a good leader.

Slide.Title: fool (verb)
Slide.SlideText: fool (verb) Definition: Definition: to make someone believe something that is not true Synonyms: Synonyms: trick; dupe; con Examples: Examples: Is it hard to fool you? She invested in the stock because the financial advisor fooled her. Sometimes, pictures can fool people. Sometimes, pictures can fool people.

Slide.Title: for (preposition)
Slide.SlideText: for (preposition) Definition: Definition: 1) something is directed at someone; 2) through space or time; 3) to be employed by Synonyms: Synonyms: 1) intended for; 2) duration; 3) employed Examples: Examples: There is a letter for you. (intended for) We were on the train for ten hours. (duration) They work for a packaging company. (employed) The road is straight for over ten miles. (duration) The road is straight for over ten miles.

Slide.Title: foreign (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: foreign (adjective) Definition: Definition: from another country; not from your own place or experience Synonyms: Synonyms: distant; unfamiliar Examples: Examples: She speaks two foreign languages. We’re going to see a foreign film tonight. Foreign countries have beautiful architecture. Foreign countries have beautiful architecture.

Slide.Title: forest (noun)
Slide.SlideText: forest (noun) Definition: Definition: large thick growth of trees Synonyms: Synonyms: woods; jungle Examples: Examples: Forests cover around 9.4% of the earth’s surface. Forests regulate the water cycle and take away harmful carbon dioxide. Brazil has one-third of the world’s rain forests. Brazil has one-third of the world’s rain forests.

Slide.Title: forgive (verb)
Slide.SlideText: forgive (verb) Definition: Definition: to excuse someone’s bad behavior; to remove guilt from a person who behaved badly Synonyms: Synonyms: pardon; excuse; absolve Examples: Examples: He wants to forgive his father for abandoning him. Is it harder to forgive or to forget? Will she forgive him for forgetting her birthday? Will she forgive him for forgetting her birthday?

Slide.Title: former (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: former (adjective) Definition: Definition: earlier in time; not now Synonyms: Synonyms: previous; past; earlier; prior Examples: Examples: Our former home was in Sweden. He saw his former employer at a conference. The Coliseum was the former arena in ancient Rome. The Coliseum was the former arena in ancient Rome.

Slide.Title: free (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: free (adjective) Definition: Definition: 1) independent; no restrictions; 2) without cost Synonyms: Synonyms: 1) unrestricted; 2) gratis Examples: Examples: He won a free car. (gratis) In 1975, Angola became a free nation. (independent) 3) She feels free. (unrestricted) She feels free.

Slide.Title: freedom (noun)
Slide.SlideText: freedom (noun) Definition: Definition: the condition of being free Synonyms: Synonyms: liberty; autonomy; independence Examples: Examples: Women in that country are fighting for their freedom. Is freedom a place or an idea? Freedom is the center of American democracy. Freedom is the center of American democracy.

Slide.Title: freeze (verb)
Slide.SlideText: freeze (verb) Definition: Definition: to become very cold; to become hard from the cold; when a liquid turns to ice Synonyms: Synonyms: solidify Examples: Examples: Water freezes at 0°Celsius. Should you always freeze fresh meat? They froze this ice cream and put toppings on it. When water freezes it becomes ice. When water freezes it becomes ice.

Slide.Title: fresh (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: fresh (adjective) Definition: Definition: 1) newly made; recently done; 2) not preserved, aged or processed Synonyms: Synonyms: 1) new; 2) wholesome Examples: Examples: Where can you get the best fresh bread? (new) Fresh food is wonderful! Fresh fruits and vegetables are good for your health. (wholesome) Fresh fruits and vegetables are good for your health.

Slide.Title: friend (noun)
Slide.SlideText: friend (noun) Definition: Definition: someone who likes and trusts another person Synonyms: Synonyms: companion; comrade; pal (informal); buddy (informal) Examples: Examples: They became friends in elementary school. We spent the weekend with friends. Friends do things together. Friends do things together.

Slide.Title: frighten (verb)
Slide.SlideText: frighten (verb) Definition: Definition: to make someone feel fear; to make someone afraid Synonyms: Synonyms: scare; terrify Examples: Examples: Severe weather frightens people. Marriage frightens some people. Scary movies will frighten the children. Scary movies will frighten the children.

Slide.Title: frightening (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: frightening (adjective) Definition: Definition: something that causes fear Synonyms: Synonyms: terrifying; alarming; fearsome Examples: Examples: Is love frightening to anyone you know? Is bungee jumping frightening or fun? This movie is frightening to the children. This movie is frightening to the children.

Slide.Title: from (preposition)
Slide.SlideText: from (preposition) Definition: Definition: 1) having a person, place or thing as a beginning; 2) at a place distant, not near; 3) because of Synonyms: Synonyms: 1) origination; 2) distance; 3) cause Examples: Examples: They’re suffering from malaria. (cause) The school is five kilometers from my home. (distance) She is going to open a gift from her boyfriend. (origination) She’s going to open a gift from her boyfriend.

Slide.Title: front (noun)
Slide.SlideText: front (noun) Definition: Definition: forward part; opposite of back; the beginning; the first part Synonyms: Synonyms: anterior; forward Examples: Examples: I like to sit in the front of the bus. Put the chair in front of the desk. They wanted a wedding picture in front of the Eiffel Tower. They wanted a wedding picture in front of the Eiffel Tower.

Slide.Title: fuel (noun)
Slide.SlideText: fuel (noun) Definition: Definition: something burned to make heat or power Synonyms: Synonyms: energy Examples: Examples: Food is fuel for our bodies. Coal and natural gas are natural fuels. Wind energy is a good example of a natural fuel. Wind energy is a good example of a natural fuel.

Slide.Title: full (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: full (adjective) Definition: Definition: containing as much as a person or thing can hold Synonyms: Synonyms: filled; bursting; stuffed Examples: Examples: The bus is full. You’ll have to wait for the next one. The fuel tank in the car is full. The streets in Tokyo are full on Saturdays. The streets in Tokyo are full on Saturdays.

Slide.Title: fun (noun)
Slide.SlideText: fun (noun) Definition: Definition: anything that’s pleasing and gives happiness Synonyms: Synonyms: amusement; enjoyment; entertainment; pleasure Examples: Examples: We had fun at Disneyland. Did you have fun over the weekend? Spending time with friends on the beach is fun. Spending time with friends on the beach is fun.

Slide.Title: funeral (noun)
Slide.SlideText: funeral (noun) Definition: Definition: a ceremony to show respect to someone who died Synonyms: Synonyms: memorial; interment; burial Examples: Examples: His funeral will be this weekend. His family showed a video of his life at his funeral. The funeral was yesterday. The funeral was today.

Slide.Title: fusion (noun)
Slide.SlideText: fusion (noun) Definition: Definition: a blending of things in one culture with another Synonyms: Synonyms: synthesis; union; combination Examples: Examples: Jazz fusion is a combination of rock and jazz. Pilates is considered a fusion of yoga and ballet. Everyone coming together is an example of fusion. Everyone coming together is an example of fusion.
